subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Should delayed SIGKILL be allowed with ancestry-and-command-class revalidation only, or must this cleanup path retain an immutable per-process launch identity before escalating?
rationale: The current check cannot distinguish an original process from a PID-reused replacement that has the same matching command class and parent ancestry; choosing the acceptable identity contract affects whether the escalation can safely terminate live Computer Use children.

options.title: Require immutable child identity
options.body: Carry a launch-specific identity such as process start time through the grace period, compare it before SIGKILL, and demonstrate the macOS app-server flow.

options.title: Accept the scoped PID-reuse risk
options.body: Retain the ancestry-and-command-class check and explicitly accept the rare possibility of killing a replacement matching child.

recommendation.title: Require immutable child identity
recommendation.body: Carry a launch-specific identity such as process start time through the grace period, compare it before SIGKILL, and demonstrate the macOS app-server flow.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Codex app-server lifecycle work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cleanup contract.
